properties.name: Intangles
properties.description:
Intangles, headquartered in Pune, is at the forefront of revolutionizing vehicle intelligence with cutting-edge technology and a shared vision for innovation. Our team of experts, with deep expertise in technology and a passion for automotive advancements, has developed a unique hardware interface powered by state-of-the-art Digital Twin technology and proprietary AI and ML-driven algorithms. Today, our platform seamlessly connects over 500,000 assets and 41,000 fleet operators across 18 countries, processing 15 trillion sensory data points annually. We enhance efficiency, safety, and sustainability in operations that drive the global economy. Our commitment remains unwavering: to redefine the future of mobility and optimize the vehicles that keep the world moving.

We leverage Digital Twin Technology to enhance vehicle and asset performance. Our device, InGenious, easily connects to vehicles or assets with an on-board diagnostic port, bypassing the need for external adjustments. By analyzing data from the Electronic Control Unit (ECU) with our proprietary algorithms, we provide actionable insights into the engine, after-treatment, brake management, battery and alternator, and air intake systems.

Our solutions are designed to predict and prevent malfunctions, saving time and maintenance costs. We offer real-time updates on fuel and DEF levels, consumption, and shrinkage, alongside fuel economy trends. Driver monitoring is simplified through our system, enabling the promotion of efficient and safe driving practices. We track over 20 driving behavior exceptions, provide live tracking, geofence alerts, and maintenance reminders, and facilitate trip optimization for better route efficiency. All these features are integrated into our all-encompassing platform, InRoute, giving you a complete 360-degree view of your assets.

# Cogent Equity

Cogent Equity is a Investment Banking company. Cogent Equity helps owners of exceptional businesses navigate the sale process with clarity and firsthand experience. They focus on representing the true value of what you have built and securing the right buyer, on the right terms. Their focus includes market positioning, operations, customer relationships, reputation, and growth potential, factors that build buyer confidence and increase sale price. Cogent Equity employs 2 people (+50.0% YoY, +1 person), founded in 2001. Headquartered in Seattle, Washington, United States.

## A

properties.name: Cogent Equity
properties.description:
Most transaction risk isn’t created during a sale process - it’s exposed by it.
 
By the time a business goes to market, many of the factors that determine value and deal certainty are already in place. We work with business owners and their advisors to evaluate those factors before the market does.
 
At Cogent Equity, we represent a limited number of companies with $1M to $10M in adjusted EBITDA, typically with long operating histories and strong underlying performance. Our focus is not just on running a process, but on ensuring the business is positioned to succeed in one.
 
This work often begins before a sale is imminent. We evaluate the business the way a sophisticated buyer would - identifying value constraints, aligning expectations, and addressing issues that would otherwise surface during diligence.
 
For advisors, the situations where it tends to be most useful to involve us are:
 
 - An owner is beginning to consider a sale in the next 1–3 years 
 - Valuation expectations are unclear or misaligned 
 - There are known or suspected issues that could impact a transaction 
 
Our perspective is shaped by firsthand experience as owners , operators, buyers, and sellers across nine different industries - allowing me to evaluate businesses the way a sophisticated buyer actually would.
 
While much of our work begins before a sale, we also represent owners through a structured, buyer-focused transaction process when the timing is right.
 
The objective is not just the right deal, but the right buyer - and a process that holds together from start to finish.

the beginning of 2016 the Ministry of Forei

properties.name: United Work
properties.description:
the beginning of 2016 the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Netherlands asked Holland Group to do a survey among Dutch companies in Turkey in order to find out if and how many were willing to employ Syrians in their organization. Approximately 90 of the 250 companies who received our questionnaire reacted positively. 

Three in four of the companies that reacted positively indicated that they were willing to sign a Letter of Intent.

As of 2016 around 700 Dutch companies do have an entity in Turkey.

The main motive for most companies (71%) willing to employ Syrian workers is that they see this as being part of their corporate social responsibility. For 54% of the companies in the survey an (temporary) increase of their workforce is the main reason to employ Syrian refugees. Four out of ten companies hope to find a solution for open positions which are difficult to fill (specialized workers) with additional Syrian workers. The ambition to expand their activities in Arabic countries, including Syria, by trade or investment in the near future is the motive for 27% of the companies willing to hire Syrians.

Via United Work Syrians with a legal status can apply for employment at one of the Dutch companies in our data base.

Depending on the skills of the candidate, length of their unemployment, and other criteria Syrians will get a training project of maximum three weeks to make them ready to start working. United Work is looking for unemployed Syrians with a legal status who are motivated and committed to start the learning, training and work program with the purpose to get back to work.

By reducing excessive speeding, harsh acceleration, and aggressive driving behaviors, fleets can lower fuel consumption, minimize wear and tear, and create a safer driving culture across their organization.

LifeSafer ISA also helps organizations strengthen compliance and risk management efforts through features like tamper detection, speed event monitoring, and automated speed control. Whether managing a service fleet, delivery operation, utility vehicles, or company trucks, ISA creates a safer and more efficient fleet environment designed to protect drivers, vehicles, and the bottom line.

entity.name: Cogent Equity
entity.description:
Most transaction risk isn’t created during a sale process - it’s exposed by it.
 
By the time a business goes to market, many of the factors that determine value and deal certainty are already in place. We work with business owners and their advisors to evaluate those factors before the market does.
 
At Cogent Equity, we represent a limited number of companies with $1M to $10M in adjusted EBITDA, typically with long operating histories and strong underlying performance. Our focus is not just on running a process, but on ensuring the business is positioned to succeed in one.
 
This work often begins before a sale is imminent. We evaluate the business the way a sophisticated buyer would - identifying value constraints, aligning expectations, and addressing issues that would otherwise surface during diligence.
 
For advisors, the situations where it tends to be most useful to involve us are:
 
 - An owner is beginning to consider a sale in the next 1–3 years 
 - Valuation expectations are unclear or misaligned 
 - There are known or suspected issues that could impact a transaction 
 
Our perspective is shaped by firsthand experience as owners , operators, buyers, and sellers across nine different industries - allowing me to evaluate businesses the way a sophisticated buyer actually would.
 
While much of our work begins before a sale, we also represent owners through a structured, buyer-focused transaction process when the timing is right.
 
The objective is not just the right deal, but the right buyer - and a process that holds together from start to finish.

entity.name: Gro Digital Platforms

Gro Digital Platforms marks the beginning of a new era in trucking in India. We provide an end-to-end digital platform for transporters, simplifying their operations and enhancing efficiency.

Founded in 2021 as a joint venture between Ashok Leyland Ltd and Hinduja Leyland Finance Ltd, Gro Digital Platforms carries the legacy of the Hinduja Group, a leader in the Indian commercial vehicle industry for over 70 years. Over this time, the group has provided services and built an extensive network of fleet owners who have become invaluable partners.

Gro Digital Platforms brings together a thriving community of fleet owners, drivers, and shippers on a single platform, offering them opportunities to scale their businesses through a variety of services.

Today, Gro powers movement across more than 3,500 transport routes, enabling over 8,000 trips per month. The platform connects more than 1,000 load providers, 21,500 validated transport partners, and a fleet of over 210,000 trucks, operating in 190+ locations across 20 Indian states. Our reach extends beyond movement — with 20,000+ fuel stations and 20,000+ mechanics in our support ecosystem, we ensure that reliability, efficiency, and cost-effectiveness are not just promises but guarantees.

At Gro, we’re not just solving problems; we’re building the future. We’re digitising the way goods move, empowering every stakeholder in the trucking value chain, and creating a smarter, scalable, and more profitable transport network for India.

Digitising the Future of Trucking. Let’s Gro, together!

entity.name: United Work
entity.description:
the beginning of 2016 the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Netherlands asked Holland Group to do a survey among Dutch companies in Turkey in order to find out if and how many were willing to employ Syrians in their organization. Approximately 90 of the 250 companies who received our questionnaire reacted positively. 

Three in four of the companies that reacted positively indicated that they were willing to sign a Letter of Intent.

As of 2016 around 700 Dutch companies do have an entity in Turkey.

The main motive for most companies (71%) willing to employ Syrian workers is that they see this as being part of their corporate social responsibility. For 54% of the companies in the survey an (temporary) increase of their workforce is the main reason to employ Syrian refugees. Four out of ten companies hope to find a solution for open positions which are difficult to fill (specialized workers) with additional Syrian workers. The ambition to expand their activities in Arabic countries, including Syria, by trade or investment in the near future is the motive for 27% of the companies willing to hire Syrians.

Via United Work Syrians with a legal status can apply for employment at one of the Dutch companies in our data base.

Depending on the skills of the candidate, length of their unemployment, and other criteria Syrians will get a training project of maximum three weeks to make them ready to start working. United Work is looking for unemployed Syrians with a legal status who are motivated and committed to start the learning, training and work program with the purpose to get back to work.

entity.description:
LifeSafer Intelligent Speed Assistance (ISA) helps fleet operators improve driver safety, reduce operating costs, and extend vehicle life by automatically keeping vehicles within posted speed limits. By reducing excessive speeding, harsh acceleration, and aggressive driving behaviors, fleets can lower fuel consumption, minimize wear and tear, and create a safer driving culture across their organization.

For fleet managers, LifeSafer ISA provides powerful telematics and GPS-based insights that support smarter fleet operations. Real-time data on speed, idle time, harsh braking, and driver behavior allows companies to identify inefficiencies, improve accountability, and make data-driven decisions that reduce overall fleet expenses while increasing operational visibility.

By encouraging smoother driving habits, ISA can significantly reduce maintenance costs tied to brakes, tires, transmissions, and engine strain — helping maximize vehicle lifecycle performance and improve long-term asset utilization. Fleets often see measurable savings in fuel spend, accident-related expenses, and unplanned downtime while improving driver retention and public safety.

LifeSafer ISA also helps organizations strengthen compliance and risk management efforts through features like tamper detection, speed event monitoring, and automated speed control. Whether managing a service fleet, delivery operation, utility vehicles, or company trucks, ISA creates a safer and more efficient fleet environment designed to protect drivers, vehicles, and the bottom line.

entity.description:
Wielu managerów transportu żyje w dwóch rzeczywistościach. Pierwsza to system GPS – wiemy, gdzie auto jest. Druga to "czarna dziura" – czyli stan techniczny, wyposażenie i realna komunikacja z kierowcą, która ginie w sms-ach, na luźnych kartkach i w Excelu.

Dlatego stworzyliśmy system, który wypełnia tę lukę. To nie jest kolejny lokalizator. To cyfrowy ekosystem operacyjny łączący Biuro, Warsztat i Kabinę Kierowcy.

Oto jak zmieniamy zasady gry w zarządzaniu flotą:

🛠️ 1. Koniec z "papierową" usterką (Advanced Fleet & Maintenance) Uszkodzenia pojazdów to koszt. Ale brak informacji o nich to koszt podwójny. Nasz system wprowadza pełny cykl życia szkody – od zdjęcia zrobionego przez kierowcę w aplikacji, przez status "Planned", aż po weryfikację "Fixed" po wyjeździe z serwisu. • Smart Inspections: Aż 7 typów protokołów (od Daily Check, przez Handover, po raporty powypadkowe). • Historia 360°: Każdy ciągnik i naczepa ma swoją cyfrową teczkę: historia napraw, przebiegi, zbliżające się terminy legalizacji i przeglądów.

👨✈️ 2. Kierowca w centrum procesu (Driver Hub & HR) Kierowca to nie tylko "rekord w bazie". To kluczowy pracownik, którego trzeba sprawnie wdrożyć i wyposażyć. • Automatyczny Onboarding: Nowy pracownik przechodzi przez cyfrową ścieżkę wdrożenia w aplikacji. Nic nie umknie. • Monitoring Uprawnień: System sam pilnuje terminów ważności prawa jazdy, badań lekarskich czy kursów, wysyłając odpowiednie Alerty z wyprzedzeniem. • Task Center: Zamiast dzwonić – przydzielasz zadania (cykliczne lub jednorazowe) bezpośrednio na telefon kierowcy i widzisz moment ich wykonania.

🦺 3. Gdzie jest ta wiertarka? (Inventory & Equipment) Ile sprzętu ginie w trasie? Wprowadziliśmy moduł Inventory, który działa jak magazyn e-commerce dla Twojej firmy. • Śledź każdy element: od ubrań roboczych, przez narzędzia, po apteczki. • Każdy przedmiot ma swój status (Nowy/Używany/Uszkodzony) i jest przypisany do konkretnej osoby lub pojazdu. • Rozliczasz kierowcę jednym kliknięciem

messages.content:
You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B benchmark.

Definition - a company lookalike API takes a seed company and returns other
companies that resemble it. Resemblance has two halves, and they are judged
DIFFERENTLY:

  ANCHOR       - who the seed sells to, and what it fundamentally is
                 (e.g. "restaurant point-of-sale platform"). This is a HARD
                 requirement. Every lookalike must be the same kind of company
                 for the same kind of customer. No amount of feature overlap
                 substitutes for it.
  CAPABILITIES - what the seed does (e.g. payments, online ordering, payroll,
                 operations). A lookalike matches ANY non-empty subset. It does
                 not need all of them, and matching more is not required to
                 qualify - only to be a closer match.

So: a true lookalike clears the ANCHOR and shares at least one CAPABILITY.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company - the company the lookalike search started from, with its
    ANCHOR and its CAPABILITIES listed separately.
  • A CANDIDATE company - a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide in this order, and do not work backwards from a conclusion:

STEP 1 - anchor_match (the gate).
  True only if the CANDIDATE is the same kind of company as the ANCHOR, for
  the same kind of customer. Ask: would someone shopping for the SEED consider
  this company to be in the same market?
    - A different customer fails, even in the same product category
      (restaurant POS vs retail-only POS: the customer differs).
    - A different category fails, even for the same customer
      (a restaurant POS vs a restaurant-supply distributor: both sell to
      restaurants, but only one is the same kind of company).
    - Serving the category rather than competing in it fails: agencies,
      consultancies, integrators, resellers.
    - Being a customer of the category fails (an actual restaurant is not a
      lookalike of a restaurant POS platform).
    - Parent/holding companies, the seed itself, and duplicate or parody
      entries fail.
  When you cannot tell what the candidate sells, anchor_match is false.

STEP 2 - capabilities_matched (the overlap).
  List the SEED capabilities this candidate also does, copying the strings
  verbatim from the SEED's list. Include a capability when the candidate
  plausibly offers it as part of its product; leave it out when you have no
  evidence. Matching a subset is normal and expected.

STEP 3 - relevant.
  relevant = anchor_match AND capabilities_matched is non-empty.
  Nothing else changes it.

Rules that apply throughout:
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. A smaller, larger, or
    differently-located company clears the anchor if it is the same kind of
    company for the same kind of customer. Ignore such metadata.
  - A shared generic taxonomy label or keyword is not an anchor match. Neither
    is a similar technology stack - tech co-signals may support a judgement but
    never establish one.
  - Judge the candidate's primary business, not a side feature.
  - When in doubt on the anchor, answer false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words: name the anchor verdict and the overlap.

Worked examples (SEED anchor -> candidate -> verdict):
  - "restaurant point-of-sale platform" [payments, online ordering, payroll]
      • a restaurant POS suite with payments and online ordering
        -> anchor true, matched [payments, online ordering], relevant true.
      • a restaurant POS with none of the listed capabilities
        -> anchor true, matched [], relevant FALSE (no overlap).
      • a retail-only POS with payments
        -> anchor FALSE (different customer), relevant false.
      • a general payments processor with no restaurant POS product
        -> anchor FALSE (different category), relevant false.
      • an actual restaurant chain
        -> anchor FALSE (customer of the category), relevant false.
      • an agency that installs restaurant POS systems
        -> anchor FALSE (serves the category), relevant false.
  - "CRM and marketing automation platform for go-to-market teams"
      • a smaller CRM with marketing automation -> anchor true, relevant true.
      • a lead-generation agency using that CRM for clients -> anchor false.
  - "digital bank for consumers"
      • a digital bank in another country -> anchor true (geography is not a
        constraint), relevant true if any capability overlaps.
  - "developer-security platform"
      • a company on a similar cloud stack selling HR software -> anchor false.

messages.content:
You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B benchmark.

Definition - a company lookalike API takes a seed company and returns other
companies that resemble it. Resemblance has two halves, and they are judged
DIFFERENTLY:

  ANCHOR       - who the seed sells to, and what it fundamentally is
                 (e.g. "restaurant point-of-sale platform"). This is a HARD
                 requirement. Every lookalike must be the same kind of company
                 for the same kind of customer. No amount of feature overlap
                 substitutes for it.
  CAPABILITIES - what the seed does (e.g. payments, online ordering, payroll,
                 operations). A lookalike matches ANY non-empty subset. It does
                 not need all of them, and matching more is not required to
                 qualify - only to be a closer match.

So: a true lookalike clears the ANCHOR and shares at least one CAPABILITY.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company - the company the lookalike search started from, with its
    ANCHOR and its CAPABILITIES listed separately.
  • A CANDIDATE company - a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide in this order, and do not work backwards from a conclusion:

STEP 1 - anchor_match (the gate).
  True only if the CANDIDATE is the same kind of company as the ANCHOR, for
  the same kind of customer. Ask: would someone shopping for the SEED consider
  this company to be in the same market?
    - A different customer fails, even in the same product category
      (restaurant POS vs retail-only POS: the customer differs).
    - A different category fails, even for the same customer
      (a restaurant POS vs a restaurant-supply distributor: both sell to
      restaurants, but only one is the same kind of company).
    - Serving the category rather than competing in it fails: agencies,
      consultancies, integrators, resellers.
    - Being a customer of the category fails (an actual restaurant is not a
      lookalike of a restaurant POS platform).
    - Parent/holding companies, the seed itself, and duplicate or parody
      entries fail.
  When you cannot tell what the candidate sells, anchor_match is false.

STEP 2 - capabilities_matched (the overlap).
  List the SEED capabilities this candidate also does, copying the strings
  verbatim from the SEED's list. Include a capability when the candidate
  plausibly offers it as part of its product; leave it out when you have no
  evidence. Matching a subset is normal and expected.

STEP 3 - relevant.
  relevant = anchor_match AND capabilities_matched is non-empty.
  Nothing else changes it.

Rules that apply throughout:
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. A smaller, larger, or
    differently-located company clears the anchor if it is the same kind of
    company for the same kind of customer. Ignore such metadata.
  - A shared generic taxonomy label or keyword is not an anchor match. Neither
    is a similar technology stack - tech co-signals may support a judgement but
    never establish one.
  - Judge the candidate's primary business, not a side feature.
  - When in doubt on the anchor, answer false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words: name the anchor verdict and the overlap.

Worked examples (SEED anchor -> candidate -> verdict):
  - "restaurant point-of-sale platform" [payments, online ordering, payroll]
      • a restaurant POS suite with payments and online ordering
        -> anchor true, matched [payments, online ordering], relevant true.
      • a restaurant POS with none of the listed capabilities
        -> anchor true, matched [], relevant FALSE (no overlap).
      • a retail-only POS with payments
        -> anchor FALSE (different customer), relevant false.
      • a general payments processor with no restaurant POS product
        -> anchor FALSE (different category), relevant false.
      • an actual restaurant chain
        -> anchor FALSE (customer of the category), relevant false.
      • an agency that installs restaurant POS systems
        -> anchor FALSE (serves the category), relevant false.
  - "CRM and marketing automation platform for go-to-market teams"
      • a smaller CRM with marketing automation -> anchor true, relevant true.
      • a lead-generation agency using that CRM for clients -> anchor false.
  - "digital bank for consumers"
      • a digital bank in another country -> anchor true (geography is not a
        constraint), relevant true if any capability overlaps.
  - "developer-security platform"
      • a company on a similar cloud stack selling HR software -> anchor false.
